clue.text: Import test to trap people

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
men means people

explanation.surface: A customs inspector tests an imported shipment in a sting to catch smugglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Import in the sense of significance or weight is a synonym for moment, as in 'of great moment'.

clue.text: 27 mirabelles drunk (only one litre)

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
only one says one of the two litre letters is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone has downed fruit brandy made from mirabelle plums, only a litre of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only one litre' drops one of the two L's from MIRABELLES; 'drunk' shuffles the rest. 27 is DOWNCAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable and downcast are synonyms, both meaning unhappy and low in spirits.

clue.text: Distribution network seen in cockpit

definitions.meaning: the network of pipes or cables supplying water, gas or electricity
a main is a cockfight, and a cockpit is a pit for cockfighting

explanation.surface: Network equipment spotted in a plane's cockpit.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockpit was originally an arena for cockfights; a main is an old word for a cockfighting match.
explanation.definitionFit: The supply pipes and cables are the mains, and mains are also cockfighting matches.

clue.text: Vacuum — it makes no difference

definitions.meaning: a vacuum contains no substance at all

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a vacuum cleaner's choice is irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum is literally empty of matter, and the phrase also means 'regardless'.

clue.text: One travelled around and devoured waste

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for travelled the other way round

parts.note: came means travelled to a place
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means devoured

explanation.surface: A wanderer comes back from a long trip, wolfs down food and wastes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'waste away'; 'around' turns the word for travelled back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make thin or waste away, a verb sense matching waste as in 'waste away'.

clue.text: French heroine exchanged for Asian model

indicators.note: exchanged means swapped about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A French heroine is swapped for a model from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc, the French national heroine, was nicknamed after the city she relieved in 1429.

clue.text: Revolutionary's key moving forward

parts.note: Che Guevara was an Argentine Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's key thing is to keep pressing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like part of 'moving forward' but is the definition; 'moving' turns KEY into EKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of presumptuous or bold means impudent, which is cheeky.

clue.text: Almost stagger over Scot resembling legendary warrior

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for stagger

parts.note: to stagger someone is to amaze them
on means over in the sense of concerning
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman nearly reels over, looking like a mythical fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a legendary race of female warriors, so amazonian means like one of them.

clue.text: Sinew not at first pointing away

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a tendon is a sinew

explanation.surface: A tendon initially not pointing in the right direction.
explanation.definitionFit: End on describes something with its end facing the viewer, pointing straight away or towards.

clue.text: Some dismiss him — "Merely a glint"

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a man's claim that what he saw was merely a faint gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: A shimmer is a faint wavering light, close in meaning to a glint or gleam.

clue.text: Hogarth's version of headway achieved in haymaking?

definitions.meaning: William Hogarth's series of eight paintings
literally the advance of a rake, the tool used in haymaking

explanation.surface: Hogarth's own take on how farmhands get on gathering hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth's painted series follows a dissolute man; literally it is a hay rake's advance.

clue.text: Composer's country

definitions.meaning: The possessive reads as his name
a nation of the British Isles, the Emerald Isle

explanation.surface: A question about which nation a composer came from.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer John Ireland shares his surname with the island nation west of Britain.

clue.text: During a break, I take over again

indicators.note: during places the I in the middle of the time taken as a break

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Someone takes over a task again in the middle of a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit an exam is to take it over again, a British usage for retaking a test.

clue.text: Very low level

definitions.meaning: a ... price is a very low one
to level a building is to flatten or demolish it

explanation.surface: A description of something at rock bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockdown describes a bargain price, and as a verb phrase knock down means to raze or level.

clue.text: Travel agency in hardware store?

definitions.meaning: a cut-price travel agent selling discounted tickets
read literally, a shop that sells buckets, as an ironmonger would

explanation.surface: Asking whether a travel agent is housed inside an ironmonger's.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucket shop is informal British for an agency selling cheap air tickets; literally a pail seller.

clue.text: When drunk, I would incline to give some lip

indicators.note: when signals the I'd being held inside, as one is in one's cups when drunk

parts.note: in one's cups means drunk
I'd is short for I would
to bow is to incline the head

explanation.surface: A tipsy person announces they'd lean over and give someone cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one's cups' is an old phrase for drunk. 'to give' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cupid's bow is the double curve of the upper lip, so it is part of a lip.

clue.text: Branch openings of local institution might be

indicators.note: openings are the starting letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the branch offices of a local institution might be opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb of a tree is one of its large branches, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Good luck in the theatre but not on the piste

definitions.meaning: actors say this to wish each other luck, since saying good luck is thought unlucky
a skier wishes no one a fractured leg on the ski slope

explanation.surface: A wish of luck that suits the stage but not a ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre folk wish luck with the idiom, but literally a skier would dread a fracture.

clue.text: PM and half his forbears amassed very little money

parts.note: William Pitt was a British Prime Minister

indicators.note: half says only the first half of the word for forbears is kept

parts.note: one's ancestry is one's forbears

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister and half his ancestors scraped together very little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps ANCE from ANCESTRY; 'his' and 'amassed' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small or meagre sum of money, such as a poor wage.

clue.text: Make out with eastern Mata Hari type

parts.note: Mata Hari was a famous First World War spy

explanation.surface: Someone getting romantically involved with an oriental femme fatale.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, which is to make out something distant.

clue.text: Bar in cell I dislodged, showing virtuosity

indicators.note: dislodged means knocked out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A prisoner shows great skill by working a bar loose from his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliance in a performer means outstanding skill, which is what virtuosity names.

clue.text: Psycho's mother has brought up murderer

parts.note: ma means mother

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Bible

explanation.surface: In the film Psycho, the mother has raised a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns CAIN into NIAC; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho and a maniac are both informal words for a violently deranged person.

clue.text: Called in evil man, needing a plant

indicators.note: in places the word for called inside the name of the villain

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll
rang means called on the phone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone phones a villain for help because they need a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a flowering shrub, a garden plant with large clustered blooms.

clue.text: Watered animal died — that's not right

indicators.note: that's not says the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: a horse is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone watered an animal and it died, which is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not right' removes R from HORSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosed means sprayed with a hosepipe, which is how one waters a garden.

clue.text: Extract from record is to follow

definitions.meaning: a single song or piece on an album

explanation.surface: A legal note that an excerpt from the record will be pursued next.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is one song on an album, and to track is to follow a trail.

clue.text: Aren't I almost sort of acid?

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: am I not is the full form of aren't I

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are almost a kind of acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins, so amino names a sort of acid.

clue.text: Sink as support is missing

indicators.note: missing means the word is is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to subsidise is to support financially
taken as written

explanation.surface: A building sinks because its foundations give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes IS from SUBSIDISE; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink lower, as ground or a building settles downward.

clue.text: Try to contact newspaper first —- it'll tell you the time

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to dial is to try to contact by phone

explanation.surface: Advice to ring the newspaper before anyone else, as they will tell you when.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial shows the hour by the shadow its pointer casts, so it tells the time.

clue.text: Despondent cads won't fool around

indicators.note: fool around means mess about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Rogues are glum because they refuse to mess about.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, a synonym of despondent.

clue.text: Take ages to fit in

definitions.meaning: to ... is to take a long time
to be at home in a group

explanation.surface: Advice that settling in somewhere takes a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, be long means take ages; as one word it means feel at home.
